subject: parameter representation in obj$simulate() vs MakeADFun

messages.author: 00f2debfd588b763
messages.subject: parameter representation in obj$simulate() vs MakeADFun
parts:
The way the parameters are represented in MakeADFun as a list and in obj$simulate() as a vector make it complicated to switch between them. 

Also obj$simulate()  only requires the estimated parameters while MakeADFun requires all the parameters.

This is all a bit confusing, particularly when combined with the confusion between obj and opt in where you are getting values from and what parameters are being used.

Does anyone have a clear and concise guide on how to use obj and opt, and how to associate them with parameters?

Thanks.

messages.author: 00f2debfd588b763
messages.subject: Re: parameter representation in obj$simulate() vs MakeADFun
parts:
Also, when the parameters are a list you don't have to worry about the order, but when they are a vector you do. The order has to be as in the cpp, not as in the list used to call 

MakeADFun

messages.subject: Re: parameter representation in obj$simulate() vs MakeADFun
parts:
by obj I mean the object returned from  MakeADFun 
by opt I mean the object returned from the optimization routine  e.g. do.call("optim",obj) or nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr, lower = bounds_lower, upper = bounds_upper)
